children: Singapore's Economic Growth Slowed in Third Quarter
SINGAPORE--Singapore's economic growth was higher than expected in the third quarter, though it slowed due to the conflict in the Middle East.

Gross domestic product grew 5.4% in the July-September quarter, compared with the same period a year earlier, according to advance estimates released Wednesday by the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry.
That compared with the revised growth of 6.2% in the second quarter and the 5.1% third quarter expansion tipped by a Wall Street Journal poll of economists.
Manufacturing output in the third quarter rose 7.5% from a year earlier, compared with a revised 12.9% expansion in the second quarter.

Growth was supported by output increases in the electronics, precision engineering, transport engineering and general manufacturing segments, which outweighed output declines in the chemicals and biomedical manufacturing segments, the ministry said.

On a seasonally adjusted quarterly basis, the economy expanded 1.1% from the previous quarter, following a revised growth of 1.5% in the second quarter and missing the 1.3% growth estimate from the WSJ poll.

Singapore has benefited from strong global investment in artificial intelligence, which has supported demand for its semiconductors and chipmaking equipment. However, disruptions stemming from the Middle East conflict have weighed on parts of the economy.

In August, the ministry raised its 2026 growth forecast to 4.5%-5.5% from 2.0%-4.0%, a better-than-expected first half and an improved outlook for the rest of the year, supported by AI-related capital expenditure.
